spec.problem: Forgot-password exposes its bearer reset token in application logs, has no delivery path, and the delivered reset URL has no learner screen.

acceptance.text: Forgot-password route renders localized accessible UI in anonymous state; invalid form input is handled; submitting valid email calls same-origin recovery API; response stays anti-enumerating; no reset token is exposed in logs or response; backend stores only token hash and safely delivers an expiring reset link through configured local mail capture; record browser/API evidence, defects and retests.

A delivered reset link opens a localized accessible password reset screen; the learner can submit a valid new password through the real reset API; token reuse or invalid input is rejected; successful reset revokes prior learner sessions and returns the learner to login.
Reset password consumes a token exactly once under concurrent requests; token consumption, password replacement, and session revocation commit atomically, and failures roll back all three changes.
AC4: Recovery API submissions work through the deployed learner-origin Next.js BFF as well as the local audit proxy; the BFF forwards request body and upstream status without logging bearer tokens.
AC5: Forgot-password preserves the supported locale in the reset email and link; email copy and reset-page language controls are localized for supported learner languages.
Password reset retains its active fragment token across unrelated hash changes such as the skip-to-content anchor, and a replacement reset token is consumed normally.
Recovery BFFs stream-limit request bodies to the Go lifecycle limit before buffering or forwarding and return a generic 413 without reading or forwarding oversized bodies.
Forgot and reset IP throttles use the rightmost validated forwarded client IP only when the Go API peer is loopback; public peers cannot spoof rate-limit keys.
Only active learner accounts are eligible for reset-token issuance and consumption; a disabled learner keeps the existing credential and token unused.

Recovery requests are committed to a bounded PostgreSQL outbox before success; saturation returns the same generic retryable service failure for any email, and claimed work survives API restart with bounded retry.
A reset submission started with token A cannot complete or clear loading/error state after the browser has switched to token B; token B remains usable.
Password-reset URLs use HTTPS for non-loopback hosts; HTTP is accepted only for local loopback development origins.
SMTP delivery returns its actual acceptance/rejection to the durable worker; locale and reset link are verified from the generated SMTP message for English, Vietnamese, and Japanese.
In React Strict Mode the emailed fragment token survives effect replay, and an expired claim already at the retry ceiling is removed without generating another token or email.
When SMTP delivery is configured, WEB_PUBLIC_URL must be explicitly supplied and validated so recovery messages cannot silently target localhost in production.

spec.expected_behavior: Reset tokens never appear in logs or HTTP responses and valid known-email requests hand a reset link to configured delivery while preserving the generic response.
spec.observed_behavior: Forgot-password stores only a hash but logs the raw token field; the UI can report success without mailing a link.
spec.rollback_plan: The outbox migration is additive. Roll back the Go API and learner BFF to the prior revision while retaining auth.password_reset_request; do not drop the table while requests may be pending. Drain or explicitly delete short-lived queued email addresses only through a reviewed maintenance procedure.

red_exception.reason: The learner-origin recovery BFF routes and locale-aware delivery boundary are new components with no compiling baseline; sensitivity mutations and reviewer-approved current-behavior tests cover them.
